subject: Staged autoscale waterfall + transient crediting matrix for Cobalt deal
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Walker <ewalker@cobalt.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@cobalt.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Staged autoscale waterfall proposal for initial Dedicated commitment

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for the deep-dive earlier. Attached is a draft we discussed outlining a staged autoscale ("waterfall") approach tied to transient credits so you get predictable baseline performance while retaining burst headroom for spikes. High-level summary below — full detail is in the attached PDF.

1) Stages and triggers (per reserved slab):
   - Baseline (Stage 0): reserved pool runs up to 70% util. No credits consumed.
   - Shoulder (Stage 1): util 70-85% triggers prewarm of ephemeral nodes (headroom x1.4). Minor credit usage.
   - Burst (Stage 2): util >85% or queued requests >120s triggers full burst (headroom x2.5). Credits consumed from transient pool.

2) Autoscale behavior and timings:
   - Scale-up cooldown: 90–120s (to avoid oscillation)
   - Scale-down delay: 10–15 minutes (preserve warm cache and KV)
   - Prewarm window: 30s before accepting additional routed traffic where possible

3) Eviction & fallback
   - Eviction preference: ephemeral previews -> best-effort preemptible -> reserved fallback.
   - Model fallback: when burst capacity unavailable, traffic is routed to an optimized smaller-quantized model to maintain latency SLOs (if agreed).

4) Crediting and billing
   - Cobalt will receive a transient credits pool tied to the first 90 days larger-burst protection (details in matrix). Credits consumed only in Stage 2.
   - Overages billed monthly; we can cap exposure per month if you prefer.

Next steps: please confirm whether the three-stage triggers look right for your traffic shape and suggest a 45-minute call to finalize thresholds and map them to your route IDs.

Attachments: staged-autoscale-proposal-v1.pdf

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side before the call:

- Can the transient credits be applied to tail-latency mitigation (i.e., using extra GPUs to reduce p99) or are they strictly for throughput?
- On the model fallback: can you confirm expected quality delta (we need to be sure not to regress below our acceptance bar for 2% of responses).

We also need an ops contact who will be paged if the cluster breaches Stage 2 for >10 minutes. Priya and I will join the call — how about Tuesday Aug 25 at 10am PT?

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Staged autoscale proposal — ops questions from Cobalt

Ben / team —

Answers below (tech details):

- p99 and Stage mapping: Stage 1 is intended as headroom for sustained shoulder traffic; it will reduce incidence of transient p99 spikes but is not an SLA-backed stage by default. If Cobalt needs a contractual p99 SLO at Stage 1, we can add an SLA article and increase reserved baseline or charge for an SLA commitment.

- Credits & tail latency: transient credits are consumed when we instantiate ephemeral nodes (Stage 2). They do reduce tail-latency by adding GPU capacity (and allowing wider batching where appropriate). We can mark a fraction of credits as "latency protection" which are prioritized for low-latency routes.

- Timers & anti-flap: scale-up cooldown 120s, scale-down 600s. Prewarm attempt starts at 30s but will only accept traffic after kernel warm completes.

- Eviction precedence and fallback model: eviction order is ephemeral (best-effort) -> preemptible -> reserved. The smaller-quantized fallback model is expected to match >98% of outputs for retrieval-augmented prompts but may have a 1–3 point BLEU/ROUGE-like delta for heavy generation tasks (we can provide eval comparisons).

Attaching the crediting matrix draft for modeling scenarios: crediting-matrix.xlsx

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

- We will map Stage triggers to specific route IDs you provide (so credits can be scoped per-route).
- For the first 90 days we will provide a transient credits pool of 10,000 token-credits dedicated to "latency protection" (applied first for routes you flag).
- We'll surface a weekly usage report and an automated alert when credit consumption reaches 60% of pool.
- If you need an SLA on p99 at Stage 1, we propose a separate addendum with a 6% uplift on reserved fee to guarantee that SLO (we can draft the language).

If that sounds reasonable, let's lock a call Aug 25 at 10am PT to finalize route mapping and produce the contract addendum draft.
